title: US Gives UN 12-Month Drawdown Window for AUSSOM Logistics Office Instead of Immediate Cutoff
detail: The United States told the UN in a diplomatic note reported September 18, 2026 that it is willing to support a 12-month drawdown followed immediately by liquidation of the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) — AUSSOM's roughly $500 million logistics backbone for fuel, medevac, food and troop transport — rather than cutting support outright. The 12-month countdown would start in January 2027, replacing Washington's earlier position (reported in July) that it would block any UN Security Council renewal of UNSOS support beyond the original December 31, 2026 deadline. A State Department spokesperson said drawdown timelines would be finalized during UN Security Council deliberations in December. Security analyst Samira Gaid warned the UNSOS shutdown could still trigger the AU mission's collapse, while Somalia expert Prof. Afyare Elmi said AUSSOM is 'a key pillar of Somalia's state' and its loss risks 'a real risk of state fragmentation.' UNSOS already began staff terminations and equipment auctions in late August under the original timeline.

media.caption: The US agreed to a 12-month wind-down of UN logistics support for AUSSOM instead of an immediate cutoff, Sep 18, 2026

title: Facebook Account Removals Hit Puntland, Jubaland Leaders and Somali Journalists
detail: A wave of Facebook account suspensions, deletions and fraudulent copyright claims targeting Somali political leaders, lawmakers, journalists and independent media outlets was reported September 18, 2026, renewing concerns over censorship of voices critical of the federal government. Affected accounts included the official pages of the Puntland and Jubaland presidents, former Puntland President Abdirahman Mohamed Mohamud Farole, government ministers, lawmakers and members of the Somali Journalists Syndicate. Tactics documented include mass-reporting campaigns, false death reports converting accounts to memorialized profiles, and copyright claims from accounts with no connection to the disputed content — one filer using the name 'The Odyssey' allegedly demanded $5,000 to withdraw a claim, per an August 2026 Syndicate investigation. The report noted a similar wave hit over 32 accounts in late 2024. Facebook remains Somalia's dominant platform for political communication and independent news distribution, making the removals a significant blow to opposition and press voices amid the ongoing federal-state political rift.

media.caption: Facebook account removals hit Puntland and Jubaland leaders, ministers and journalists critical of the federal government, Sep 18, 2026
